commitResults.messageBody:
Luke.main currently handles input control, command dispatch, task
creation, and completion updates in one long method. This obscures the
top-level interaction flow and duplicates related command details.

Extract focused helpers so main reads at one level of abstraction.
Centralize task addition and task-number parsing to keep related state
updates together while preserving existing behavior and output.

Move command-word and task-number parsing out of Luke so that Parser owns command syntax interpretation. This keeps Luke focused on application flow, removes duplicated parsing responsibilities, and preserves existing behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle unrecognized commands without adding tasks
commitResults.messageBody: Remove the misleading behavior that stored unrecognized commands as generic tasks. Unknown commands now produce a user-facing message through Ui while leaving the task list unchanged.

Add a project-specific fail-fast UI regression testing skill and Level-4 test plan covering Todo, Deadline, Event, listing, marking, and unmarking. Update agent instructions so the UI test plan is reviewed and the test-ui skill is invoked after production code changes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Improve Java documentation and coding standards
commitResults.messageBody: Expand the project Java coding-standard guidance using the SE-EDU basic and intermediate conventions while preserving the CS2113 switch indentation convention. Add missing class and public-method Javadocs to the current task and UI classes. The changes preserve application behavior, DocLint reports no errors, and all 6 UI regression tests pass.

commitResults.messageBody:
TaskList currently exposes its fixed backing array, allowing callers to replace stored entries without updating taskCount.

Return a copy limited to populated slots so the array strategy remains intact while callers cannot mutate structural state.

The application never creates an untyped task, while each subtype repeats part of the common display format.

Make Task abstract and centralize type, status, and description formatting behind a protected subtype hook. Preserve all existing CLI output.
Cover malformed structured commands and invalid task indices. Verify that rejected commands preserve task state and allow the CLI to continue.
Correct spacing and Javadoc sentences, and define a serial version identifier so Java 25 compilation remains warning-free.
Remove an unnecessary unary-plus expression from TaskList while preserving the exact user-facing validation message.

commitResults.messageBody: Configure the Shadow plugin and the Luke entry point so the application can be distributed as a self-contained JAR. Add the Gradle wrapper to make the build reproducible with Java 25.
Luke currently creates and reads from Scanner directly. Let Ui own standard-input handling so the application coordinator no longer performs user-interface work.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use Ui instance for application output
commitResults.messageBody: Ui display methods are currently global static operations. Route output through the Ui instance so commands can receive one cohesive user-interface dependency.
Command behavior currently resides in Luke's dispatch switch. Introduce command objects for the existing operations so parsing and orchestration can be separated in the following increments.
Parser currently exposes separate helpers while Luke decides which behavior to run. Make Parser construct the appropriate command so command recognition has one owner.
Luke currently contains the command dispatch and execution logic. Delegate those responsibilities to Parser and Command so Luke only manages application lifecycle and shared components.
The regression plan expects wording that differs from the existing application output. Record the established wording so the plan detects real behavioral regressions during the OOP refactor.
Integrate command objects and move user interaction into Ui so Luke serves as the application coordinator.
Date parsing and display will be needed by multiple task types. Centralize the accepted and user-facing formats so deadlines and events use one consistent definition.
Deadline dates are currently unchecked text. Parse strict yyyy-MM-dd input into LocalDate, show a friendly date, and persist the machine-readable ISO value.
Event boundaries are currently unchecked text. Parse strict date-time input, reject non-increasing ranges, display friendly values, and retain ISO-compatible storage.
LocalDateTime's default text cannot be parsed by Luke's accepted input format. Save events with the shared storage formatter and report malformed stored records as load failures instead of crashing.
Typed dates introduce validation paths that the existing UI plan does not exercise. Record invalid calendar dates, formats, and non-increasing event ranges as regression cases.
TaskList currently supports only indexed task operations. Add case-insensitive keyword matching that preserves task order so commands can query descriptions without exposing the internal collection.
Search results need a command-level workflow and consistent rendering. Add FindCommand to query TaskList without saving and let Ui handle matching and empty-result output.
Parser does not yet expose the new search behavior to users. Parse find keywords into FindCommand and reject empty searches with a specific user-facing error.
The UI plan does not yet protect search behavior. Add cases for ordered multiple matches, case-insensitive matching, no results, missing keywords, and an unchanged task list.
Integrate typed deadline dates and event date-times with strict validation, friendly display formatting, and persistent storage support.
Integrate case-insensitive task-description search through the command architecture, including empty and no-match handling.
TaskList exposes the application's main collection operations without explaining their one-based numbering, return values, or failures. Document those contracts and the task-type icon abstraction.
The find-keyword parser and text-logo helper contain reusable behavior that is not obvious from their callers. Document their inputs, results, and validation contract.

JavaDoc reports undocumented implicit constructors for command types and Parser. Make command construction explicit and prevent instantiation of the all-static parser so the generated API describes the intended contracts.
Integrate complete JavaDoc coverage for task operations, parsing helpers, UI helpers, and command construction contracts.
LukeException inherits Java serialization without declaring a version identifier, which produces a lint warning. Define a stable serialVersionUID so Java 25 lint compilation is clean.
Define a stable serialization version for LukeException and remove the Java 25 lint warning.
LukeException is not persisted or exchanged through Java serialization in this application. Remove the unused version field to keep the exception class focused on its user-command error role.
Add the repository-local writing and validation workflow so future user-guide changes follow a consistent structure.
Replace the template with task-oriented setup, command, persistence, troubleshooting, and reference documentation based on the implemented CLI behavior.
Publish the validated CLI documentation and retain its reusable repository-local authoring workflow.
